share_cap.E: Equals the Rs 10 lakh working capital in the case: the FPO is running on its share capital alone

board.E: Case: nine-member board with one woman director (C = board, D = women)

usd.E: Case background: US$1 million a year for 3 to 5 years

fx.E: [S13] Rupee at 94.8 to 95.95 per USD in Aug to Sep 2026; 95 used

years.E: Case allows 3 to 5; we plan 5 with a go/no-go checkpoint at end of Year 2

new_women.A: New women members added by Year 5
new_women.E: Enrolled through JEEViKA self-help groups already active in these villages [S10]; about 30 a year

active.A: Members who sell produce through the FPO
active.E: [S9] SRIJAN raised members selling to their FPOs to 39% in 2 years; we allow 5 years plus input credit tied to sales. Vegetables lower because of daily, small lots

area.E: [S11] 83% of Bihar holdings are under 1 ha. Maize is the main rabi crop in Kosi; vegetables are grown on small plots

yield.E: [S11] Bihar maize about 4 t/ha, rabi higher. Vegetables: 15 t/ha a season x 1.5 seasons (our assumption)

mkt.A: Share of output that is sold
mkt.E: Maize is a cash crop; vegetables lose some to home use and damage [S12]

capture.A: Share of a selling member's output the FPO handles
capture.E: Input credit repaid in produce and assured payment in 7 days pull volume; vegetables lower because of side-selling to local markets

price.E: [S14] Maize MSP Rs 2,400/qtl but Bihar has no state maize procurement; Purnia mandi near Rs 2,100 to 2,300. Vegetables: blended Rs 14/kg (our assumption)

inp_users.A: Members buying inputs through the FPO
inp_users.E: [S9] SRIJAN reached 88% of shareholders buying inputs; 70% used

inp_spend.A: Input spend per member per year
inp_spend.E: Seed, fertiliser and crop protection for 0.4 ha maize or 0.2 ha vegetables (our assumption)

inp_wallet.A: Share of that spend bought from the FPO
inp_wallet.E: Fertiliser licence and bulk buying; half, not all

nursery.E: Vegetable FPOs run a shade-net nursery (also a flood fallback: seedlings can be replanted fast)

m_prod.E: Maize: about Rs 65/qtl spread on bulk contracts. Vegetables: grading premium and lower loss [S12: 4.9% to 11.6% vegetable loss]

hold.A: Share of maize held in storage for later sale
hold.E: [S15] Small farmers sell in distress at harvest; larger farmers hold 3 to 4 months

m_store.A: Net gain on stored maize after rent, interest and shrinkage
m_store.E: Assumes about 9% to 10% price rise in 4 months less about 5% holding cost; e-NWR pledge loan pays for the stock [S7]

m_inp.E: Dealer margin on bulk seed and fertiliser (our assumption)

svc_fee.E: Rs 40/qtl charged on FPO volume and on traders' maize

svc_mult.A: Third-party volume as a multiple of own volume
svc_mult.E: Dryer and godown rented out to non-members in spare weeks

cold_fee.E: Pay-per-crate service, as in the Ecozen/Oorja model in Muzaffarpur [S8]

m_today.E: Small trading and input margins at current scale (our assumption)

ceo.E: Rs 30,000 a month. Govt management cost norm is Rs 18 lakh over 3 years = Rs 6 lakh a year for all costs [S2]

staff.E: One full-time assistant; vegetables need extra grading help

fedfee.A: Fee to federation for accounts, compliance and market desk
fedfee.E: Shared chartered accountant, audit, ROC filings and sales desk; cheaper than each FPO hiring its own

om.A: Upkeep and insurance of FPO assets
om.E: Share of asset cost per year; solar cold rooms and crates wear faster

capex.E: See Infra sheet. Maize stores in leased PACS godowns, so its kit is small

g_gov.E: [S6] MIDH pays 35% of cost for post-harvest units in general areas

g_own.E: [S5] AIF requires at least 10% borrower contribution

rate.E: [S5] About 9% bank rate less 3% AIF interest subvention

tenor.E: [S5] AIF subvention runs up to 7 years

wc_pct.A: Peak working capital as share of yearly produce sales
wc_pct.E: Maize is one big rabi buying season with 30 to 60 day buyer payment; vegetables turn over within days

credit_pct.A: Share of input sales given on credit to members

match.E: [S2] Govt matches share capital up to Rs 2,000 per member, cap Rs 15 lakh per FPO

match_cap.A: Matching equity grant cap per FPO

fund_share.A: Share of the remaining gap met by the federation fund
fund_share.E: Rest from banks and NBFCs, made willing by the first-loss deposit and govt credit guarantee [S4]

vol.G: Sellers x area x yield x share sold x FPO share

cost.A: Full running cost without any grant

cover.A: Share of running cost the FPO covers itself
cover.G: Exit test: at least 100% for two years in a row

be_to.A: Turnover needed to break even at Year 5 margins
be_to.G: Running cost / income per rupee of turnover

mult.A: Year 5 turnover as a multiple of today

w_prod.A: Peak cash tied up in produce buying
w_prod.F: Stored maize is financed separately by e-NWR pledge loans [S7]

w_match.F: [S2] Free money most FPOs leave unclaimed; needs clean share register

w_capex.A: Less own share of asset kit

k1.A: Drying yard, tarpaulins, moisture meter, scale, sampling kit
k1.F: Meets ethanol and feed-mill moisture specs (14% or lower)

k2.A: Mobile maize dryer share and cleaner/grader
k2.F: One mobile dryer shared by two FPOs

k3.A: PACS godown upgrade to WDRA standard (raised stacking, fumigation, fire kit)
k3.F: [S16] Lease idle PACS godowns (Bihar built 6,158 with 16.9 lakh t) instead of building new

k5.A: Pack shed with grading tables on raised plinth
k5.F: Built above the local high-flood level

k6.A: Three village collection points and 2,000 crates

k7.F: Seedlings for replanting after floods; sold to members

lev.A: Asset value per rupee of Foundation grant

f_c2.A: Cohort 2 business as a share of cohort 1 in Year 5
f_c2.D: 24 FPOs at 60% of a cohort 1 FPO each (they join later: 6 in Y1, 18 in Y3)

f_fin.A: Accounts and compliance (CA on retainer + 2 accountants)

f_var.A: Extra servicing cost per FPO beyond 12

f_fees.D: Rs 1.2 lakh per FPO, already inside each FPO's running cost

f_share.A: Share of maize sold through federation contracts

f_comm.D: Earned from better price on 1,000 t+ lots

f_inpm.D: Federation buys seed and fertiliser in bulk for all FPOs

f_lent.A: Average amount lent out by the revolving fund
f_lent.D: Fund share of the working capital gap of both cohorts

f_util.A: Share of fund lent out on average
f_util.D: Below 100% on purpose: the flood window is kept liquid

f_rate.D: [S4] Below the 14% to 15% NBFC rate for FPO loans

f_loss.A: Loan loss and running cost of the fund

b_mkt.A: Market desk, buyer onboarding, quality testing, certification
b_mkt.I: Desk moves onto the federation payroll from Year 4, paid by its commission

b_didi.A: Women procurement agents (2 per FPO) start-up stipend
b_didi.I: Paid by FPO commission from Year 3; 24 women earn on volume

b_fund.A: Revolving fund capital (owned by the federation)
b_fund.I: Sized to the gap left after the govt matching equity grant; lent and repaid, never spent

b_fldg.I: Unlocks bank lines; returns to the federation if unused

b_cont.A: Flood contingency window in the fund
b_cont.I: Emergency loans after a flood; kept liquid

b_infra.A: Asset kits co-funded with AIF and MIDH
b_infra.I: From Infra sheet: 60% in Year 1, 40% in Year 2

b_mgmt.I: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20%, 0% of salary; FPO margin takes over

b_sys.A: Accounting software, compliance clean-up, board training
b_sys.I: Front-loaded: one-time clean-up of share registers and filings

b_women.A: Women membership drive, leadership fellowship, creche at centres
b_women.I: 150 new women members per FPO via SHGs; fellows stand for board seats

b_clim.A: Climate: flood alerts, resilient seed trials, BRFSY claims help
b_clim.I: Bihar left PMFBY; farmers must be helped to claim state aid [S17]

b_kap.A: KAP field team (business, finance, gender, climate leads)
b_kap.I: Peaks while KAP still has the govt CBBO fee, then shrinks as the federation takes over

b_fed.I: Foundation pays most of the running cost in Years 2 and 3; federation pays itself by Year 5

b_eval.I: Baseline, mid-term at the Year 2 checkpoint, endline

b_coh2.A: Playbook, kits, salary taper, fund access for cohort 2
b_coh2.I: What is left after cohort 1 is fully funded; see cost per FPO-year below

c1_cost.A: Cohort 1 cost per FPO per year

c2_cost.A: Cohort 2 cost per FPO per year
c2_cost.I: About 75% of cohort 1: desk, fund and federation already exist. Govt pays a CBBO Rs 5 lakh per FPO a year [S2]

farmers.A: Farmer members reached in Year 5 (both cohorts)

per_farmer.A: Cost per farmer member over 5 years

t_sell.A: Members selling through FPO (maize / veg avg)
t_sell.F: [S9] SRIJAN: 39% after 2 years. Today: our estimate (case: weak engagement)

t_to.F: [S3] 1,135 of 8,961 scheme FPOs (12.7%) crossed Rs 1 crore in FY25

t_cov.F: [S1] About one third of FPOs viable (ICAR-NIAP), i.e. 4 of 12. Target 6 of 12, and all 12 above 85%

t_wdir.F: [S10] FPOs with female or mixed leadership survive past support 4 to 13 points more often

t_bank.A: FPOs with a bank or NBFC credit line
t_bank.F: [S4] Only 30% of FPOs got bank loans; those with credit: 61% profitable without support vs 43%

t_fed.A: Federation covers its own running cost

c1.A: Budget each year equals Rs 950 lakh (USD 1m at Rs 95)

c3.A: Infra funding stack adds to kit cost

c4.A: Infra in budget equals Infra sheet

c5.A: Case: share capital equals working capital available

c6.A: Working capital sources add to gap

c7.A: Fund capital covers what is lent out (0 if yes)

c8.A: Federation covers its running cost (0 if yes)

flood.A: Flood year: vegetables lose 1 of 1.5 seasons
